Philosophy

Borrow Fire, Then Become Fire

Borrow the fire of intelligence; through practice, develop understanding, judgment, creation, and the capacity to keep becoming.

The argument moves from acquiring capability to cultivating a person, through finite inquiry, cooperation, and realization, then into lived feedback and shared creation. Capacities can be internalized or reliably distributed across person, models, and tools. Yinyang is one developed philosophical and working form within it.

Starting point: borrowed fire and the becoming of agents

Preview the argument, establish value and agency, give cultivation its conditional rationale through super-cuteness, then embody that direction in Baby Heraclitus.

01

Stealing fire: from borrowed fire toward generation

Begin with available intelligence: borrow fire, then develop understanding, creation, and action.

02

Personal-First Humanism

Make the ethical premise explicit: tools and cooperation support concrete lives; output volume does not substitute for development.

03

Why Write a Personal Philosophy?

First define an agent, then ask why scattered capacities need shared direction: write the actual participants and relationship into the arrangement.

04

The Argument from Super-Cuteness

First establish when openness, shared learning, and guidance support adaptation, giving the baby’s cultivation a rationale.

05

Baby Heraclitus: What kind of agent do we want to cultivate?

Then give this baby a Heraclitean character: remain open, judge, create, and change through encounters.

Understanding: finite inquiry in a changing world

Make understanding corrigible: move from representation and time into reasoning, connect conflict, view selection, and support through the preference harness, then examine finite abstraction.

06

World, process, and expression

Distinguish world, process, model, and expression so representations guide action and meet correction.

07

The stream and time

Examine different rhythms of change, memory, and experience, preserving continuity and room for revision.

08

Reasoning within an unfinished stream

Form questions, candidate explanations, and checkable inferences; distinguish retaining material from accepting a view.

09

A preference harness: rules and preferences working together

Connect preferences, rules, and evidence: choose possibilities to develop, examine their support, and revise through conflict and consequences.

10

Finite inquiry and economical abstraction

Choose useful abstractions under finite information and time, distinguishing formal results from worldly explanation.

Encounter: making shared participation possible

Develop the agent concept into reciprocal generation and actual participation, preserving human initiative and model contributions.

11

Yinyang and Taiji: ceaseless transformation

Use Sun, Moon, paired fish, and Earth to express reciprocal generation and the independent consequences of creations.

12

Participation, access, and support

Connect understanding, expression, and available action through support that preserves human initiative.

Formation: from human agency to personal philosophy and practice

Human agency is the starting point: an existing agent draws on generative capabilities to develop a personal philosophy, worldview, and sustainable form of living.

13

Literary Programming

Condense understanding through characters, imagery, and relationships, then unfold it through instructions and tools.

14

Metaphor, Analogy, and Personal Self-Revision

Develop metaphor into analogy and relation maps, distribute cognition across models, records, and tools, and revise that organization.

15

Writing a sinthome: forming a personal philosophy

Begin with a person who already perceives, generates, and acts; expand capacities with models and form a personal philosophy and the environment that sustains it.

Focused branch: Speaking, self-description, and signifying chains

Focused branch: Machines and Becoming: An Encounter with Deleuze and Guattari

Begin your own practice

Begin with the getting-started guide and ask a model to help form and realize your arrangement. Return to conceptual reading by question; completing the series is not a prerequisite.

Explore the creation method

Practice: becoming fire through environment and feedback

Begin your own practice, then enter its three environmental forms, experimental feedback, and further creation with others.

16

Trinity: Philosophy, Psychology, and Engineering in One Practice

Connect philosophy, psychology, and personal environment in a loop where experience renews understanding and practice.

17

Embodied Experimental Philosophy

Bring works into embodied life; use practice and reflection to revise explanations, boundaries, and aims.

18

Begin with this example, and make something of your own

Offer the practice to another creator: adopt, combine, or write a philosophy and form of your own.
